subject: Model fit / evals follow-up + Redwood-verified benchmarks
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit / evals follow-up + Redwood-verified benchmarks

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the immediate next steps we discussed: 

1) Summary of needs
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support summaries + safetext extraction (avg. input ~700 tokens, peak ~2k)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for short inference (<=256 tokens); p99 target for longer batches needs discussion
- Throughput target: sustained ~300 TPS for embeddings/intent routing, burst for generation up to ~80 concurrent streams

2) Recommended starting model(s)
- rw-vanguard-1.0 (Redwood-verified; 16-bit quantized profile): best balance of cost/quality for summaries, strong safety baseline
- llama3-70b-quant (latency-optimized variant): if you need higher LLM capability for complex instruction tasks; expect higher GPU footprint

3) Benchmarks + prompt sets
- Attached: redwood_model_benchmarks_030326.pdf (end-to-end TPS, latency percentiles by sequence length, and throughput curves)
- Sharing prompt sets and eval harness: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/reports/ACME-2026-03-model-fit and Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/share/1a2b3c/prompt-sets/acme-eval
- Included sample prompt set attached: acme_prompt_set_sample.jsonl (small subset of your anon transcripts we discussed)

4) Quality/regression concerns and mitigations
- We flagged two potential regressions on the sample eval: hallucination increase on rare entity extraction and a 2-3% drop in exact-match on policy-specific extracts compared to your baseline model.
- Immediate mitigation: we recommend a small prompt engineering pass + safety-templating; longer-term: we can run a quantization-aware re-eval and suggest a different kernel profile (we noted better 99th pctl latency for rw-vanguard when run with kernel set B).

5) Next steps / action items
- Dylan: run the full Acme prompt set against rw-vanguard and llama3-70b-quant; share full benchmark report (ETA: EOD Mon 30 Mar) - attached link above
- Marissa: follow up with procurement on standard T&Cs and any PO templates
- Sam: share a redacted sample of the 2k-token transcripts (if okay) and confirm whether we should include on-prem Private deployment in scope

If that matches your view, I can schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the benchmark PDF and prioritize the mutual action plan.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[dylan_brooks@redwood.ai]

Attachments: redwood_model_benchmarks_030326.pdf, acme_prompt_set_sample.jsonl

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit / evals follow-up + Redwood-verified benchmarks

Thanks Dylan — very helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we can scope the eval: 

- For the p99 latency numbers in the PDF, are those measured at production concurrency (we expect ~80 concurrent generation streams) or single-stream? We care most about 99th for the long 2k-token cases.
- Can you provide the HubSpot/Jira link to the full test harness so our infra can triage?

Also, we want to make sure the procurement folks see the tradeoffs between rw-vanguard and llama3-70b-quant. If rw-vanguard gives us similar quality with materially better latency/TCO, procurement will prefer that.

I can send a redacted set of transcripts (we'll remove PII) - planning to circulate by Monday. We'll also confirm whether Private deployment is required (probable for some customers).

Sam Taylor
Head of Product, Acme AI
sam.taylor@acme.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit / evals follow-up + Redwood-verified benchmarks

Sam —

Answers inline and next actions below.

> For the p99 latency numbers in the PDF, are those measured at production concurrency (we expect ~80 concurrent generation streams) or single-stream?

The p99s in the attached PDF are measured under a realistic concurrency profile we simulated to match the ~80-stream burst you mentioned (we ran a synthetic mix: 60 short requests, 20 long 2k requests, sustained for 10 minutes). For rw-vanguard-1.0 the observed numbers were:
- p50: 48ms (<=256 token requests)
- p95: 210ms
- p99: 420ms (2k-token heavy tail)

For llama3-70b-quant the p99 was ~680ms under the same mix, which is why we flagged latency tradeoffs in the doc. Those numbers are in the "Latency percentiles by seq len" section on page 6 of the PDF and in the Drive report.

> Can you provide the HubSpot/Jira link to the full test harness so our infra can triage?

Yes - full harness, runner configs, and perf scripts are here: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/harnesses/ACME-2026-03 (also linked in the Drive folder). I'll grant your infra team read access today - Marissa will confirm permissions.

Next actions: 
- I'll kick off the full run vs your full prompt set tonight and share the raw run artifacts + annotated regression notes by EOD Mon 30 Mar.
- If you want, we can schedule a brief 30-min call Tue 31 Mar (10am PT) to walk through regressions and mutual action plan.

I'll also include a short README for the eval runner so your infra can re-run locally if needed.

Thanks - feel free to loop in procurement threads and I'll add Marissa as the contact for PO/T&Cs.

Dylan
